title: De los nombres botánicos aztecas
author: Blas Pablo Reko
summary: An essay by physician and ethnobotanist Blas Pablo Reko arguing against Safford's claim that teonanácatl was a fanciful name for peyote. Reko insists teonanácatl was a real mushroom still eaten by Indigenous communities in Oaxaca.
excerpt: "Div. géneros de hongos, especialmente un hongo negro que crece sobre estiércol y produce efectos narcóticos" ("Various genera of mushrooms, especially a black mushroom that grows on dung and produces narcotic effects").
citation: Reko, Blas Pablo. "De los nombres botánicos aztecas." El México Antiguo 1, no. 5 (December 1919): 113–157.

draft.rationale: First twentieth-century scholar to argue in print that teonanácatl was a surviving, living mushroom cult rather than a historical curiosity or a synonym for peyote; the direct ancestor of the Weitlaner-Johnson-Schultes-Wasson rediscovery chain the archive already documents in part.

textSource.scope: Secondhand quotation of Reko (1919) as reproduced, with citation to El México Antiguo vol. 1, no. 5, in Guzmán/Ott-derived secondary literature (Erowid's 'Mushroom Pioneers,' ch. 1, archived copy). Original journal issue not located in digitized form; no direct page image or OCR of the 1919 article itself was obtained.

textQuality.notes: The Spanish sentence is quoted, with a pinpoint citation to pp. 113-157 of El México Antiguo vol. 1 no. 5, by two independent secondary sources (Erowid's Mushroom Pioneers essay and Schultes 1940's own bibliography, which cites the same volume/pages). Not verified against a page image of the original 1919 journal, which could not be located on Internet Archive, HathiTrust, or the Mexican Hemeroteca Nacional Digital. A German-cousin work by Victor A. Reko (no relation confirmed) is sometimes conflated with Blas Pablo Reko in secondary sources; this record concerns Blas Pablo Reko only.
